title: Banking platform consolidation — Enterprise on-premise migration
summary: Migrating a 93-node Platinum-licensed cluster to a 16-ERU Enterprise architecture while holding a 395-day retention requirement — and cutting storage footprint along the way.

sections.challenge: ICBC's on-premise Elasticsearch platform ran on a 93-node Platinum-licensed cluster supporting banking operations with a strict 395-day audit-log retention requirement. The licensing model and node footprint had grown without a consolidation plan, and a migration to an Enterprise licensing model was needed without compromising retention or compliance posture.
sections.architecture: The 93-node Platinum cluster was redesigned around an Enterprise licensing model sized at 16 ERUs (Elastic Resource Units), consolidating compute while preserving the full 395-day retention window required for financial-services audit trails.
sections.implementation: LogsDB was adopted as the storage layer for the consolidated architecture, reducing on-disk footprint by 30.75% relative to the prior storage approach, without shortening the mandated 395-day retention period.
sections.results: The cluster was consolidated from 93 nodes to a 16-ERU Enterprise architecture (-83%), with LogsDB delivering a 30.75% storage reduction — all while holding the 395-day retention requirement intact for compliance.
lessons: Licensing-model consolidation (Platinum nodes → Enterprise ERUs) and storage-format change (LogsDB) are separate levers — measuring them independently made the -83% and -30.75% figures each defensible on their own.
A hard compliance constraint (395-day retention) is a useful forcing function: it ruled out any storage optimization that traded away retention window.
On-premise consolidation at this scale benefits from sequencing licensing migration before storage-format changes, not the reverse.
